skill.name: upgrading-expo
skill.description: Guide Expo SDK upgrades with planning, dependency updates, configuration migration, and testing checks.
skill.summary: Helps upgrade Expo SDK versions with practical migration steps and validation guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline command names, and GitHub source links. The skill provides Expo upgrade guidance and does not contain executable scripts, prompt injection instructions, or data exfiltration intent. Package manager commands can affect projects, so users should run them with normal project safeguards.

remediation.issue: Command examples can modify dependencies and install packages.
remediation.suggestion: State that users should approve package manager commands and run them from a feature branch with version control available.

static_findings.snippet: - Use `expo install` instead of `npm install` for Expo packages
- Test on both iOS and Android

finding_verdicts.reason: This is a Markdown bash example for expected Expo upgrade commands, not Ruby backtick execution or hidden command execution. The commands are visible package manager steps for the stated purpose.
The detected line closes the Markdown code fence and does not execute anything. It is documentation syntax rather than a runtime command surface.
This is another Markdown bash example showing Expo doctor and install commands for dependency checks. No dynamic interpolation, shell wrapper, or concealed execution logic is present.
The detected line is Markdown formatting that ends a code block. It is not executable skill code and has no command injection path.
The inline command name documents a normal Expo package management recommendation. It is not a shell execution primitive or a request to run hidden commands.
The inline app.json reference is documentation about configuration files, not command execution. The surrounding section describes migration tasks without suspicious automation.
The URL appears in front matter as a source link to the Expo skill repository. There is no code that sends data to the URL or retrieves remote content automatically.
The URL is a user-facing resource link to the same Expo repository. It is not a network call, webhook, or data exfiltration channel.
The line says to test on iOS and Android as part of app validation. This is normal mobile QA guidance, not host reconnaissance or system inventory collection.

content.value_statement: Expo SDK upgrades can break dependencies, configuration, and native behavior. This skill gives a structured upgrade plan with checks for packages, app settings, APIs, and testing.
actual_capabilities: Outlines pre-upgrade checks for Expo SDK releases and breaking changes.
Provides visible Expo CLI steps for updating Expo and compatible packages.
Guides dependency conflict review with Expo doctor and compatible installs.
Highlights configuration, API, and native dependency migration tasks.
Recommends validation across core features, native modules, iOS, Android, and builds.
limitations: Does not include SDK-specific release notes or version-by-version migration details.
Does not automatically inspect project files without agent action.
Does not replace app-specific testing, native build validation, or store submission checks.
Assumes an Expo managed or Expo-compatible React Native project.

use_cases.title: Plan a Production Upgrade
use_cases.description: Create a staged Expo SDK upgrade checklist before changing dependencies in a released app.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Team Migration Work
use_cases.description: Turn Expo release changes into assigned tasks for dependencies, configuration, code updates, and testing.

use_cases.title: Prepare Upgrade Validation
use_cases.description: Define what to test after an Expo SDK update, including native modules, runtime behavior, and builds.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Upgrade Checklist
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for one Expo app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the upgrading-expo skill to create a checklist for upgrading my Expo app from SDK [current version] to SDK [target version]. Include planning, dependency updates, configuration checks, and testing.

prompt_templates.title: Review Dependency Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the upgrading-expo skill to review my Expo SDK upgrade risks. Focus on third-party packages, peer dependency warnings, Expo package compatibility, and what I should verify before merging.

prompt_templates.title: Guide Configuration Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate migration work after dependency updates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the upgrading-expo skill to guide the configuration part of my upgrade. Identify app configuration areas, native dependency considerations, deprecated options, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Release Upgrade Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced team rollout for a production app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the upgrading-expo skill to design a release-ready Expo SDK upgrade plan for a production app. Include sequencing, risk areas, owner responsibilities, test coverage, rollback planning, and final approval checks.

output_examples.input: I need to upgrade an Expo production app to a newer SDK.
output_examples.output: A staged plan covering release notes, a feature branch, dependency compatibility, configuration review, API migration, and device testing.

output_examples.input: My Expo upgrade has dependency warnings after the package update.
output_examples.output: A triage checklist that separates Expo packages, third-party packages, peer dependency warnings, and follow-up validation tasks.

output_examples.input: We need QA coverage for an Expo SDK migration.
output_examples.output: A validation plan for core flows, native modules, runtime errors, iOS behavior, Android behavior, and app store build readiness.

best_practices: Create a feature branch and keep a restorable project state before changing SDK dependencies.
Review Expo release notes and migration guides before updating packages.
Test app behavior on iOS, Android, and production-like builds before merging.
anti_patterns: Upgrade directly on the main branch without a rollback path.
Ignore peer dependency warnings or package compatibility messages.
Assume a successful local launch means app store builds will pass.

faq.question: What does this skill help me upgrade?
faq.answer: It helps plan and execute Expo SDK upgrades for Expo and React Native projects.

faq.question: Does it run package manager commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and visible command steps that should be approved before execution.

faq.question: Can it replace Expo release notes?
faq.answer: No. Use it with the official release notes and migration guides for the target SDK version.

faq.question: Does it cover dependency conflicts?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends checking third-party package compatibility and resolving peer dependency warnings.

faq.question: What should I test after upgrading?
faq.answer: Test core flows, native modules, runtime errors, iOS behavior, Android behavior, and app store builds.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Mobile developers, engineering leads, and QA teams can use it to structure Expo SDK upgrade work.
